data.long_meaning: The name Sidharth is derived from the Sanskrit word 'sidh' meaning 'accomplished' or 'perfect' and 'arth' meaning 'goal'. The name Sidharth is believed to signify an achiever of goals or someone who has accomplished a great deal. The name Sidharth carries the meaning “Achiever of Goals” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sidharth usually hope their child will grow to embody achiever of goals and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Sidharth is believed to have spiritual significance in Hinduism. It is said to represent the journey of an individual from worldly desires to spiritual enlightenment. The name is associated with the god Vishnu and is believed to bring good fortune and prosperity.
data.etymology: Sidharth belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Achiever of Goals.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sidharth total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sidharth holds great cultural significance in the Hindu tradition as it is believed to be the birth name of Lord Buddha, the founder of Buddhism. This philosopher, monk, and teacher lived in ancient India, around the 5th or 4th century BCE. The life and teachings of Lord Buddha have had a profound impact on the religious, social, and cultural development of India and have also influenced various other Eastern and Western religious and philosophical traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sidharth holds spiritual significance as it suggests someone who has attained the ultimate goal or enlightenment. In Hindu tradition, Sidharth is considered the name of a spiritual achiever, someone who has fulfilled their worldly as well as spiritual aspirations, and has attained self-realization and liberation from the cycle of birth and death. This name resonates with the spirit of determination, self-discipline, and spiritual growth, inspiring those who carry it to strive towards their goals and seek inner peace and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sidharth: One who has accomplished or achieved their goals, a seeker of enlightenment on the path to self-realization. Symbolizes determination and the pursuit of inner wisdom.

historical_references.context: Sidharth was a name used by Emperor Ashoka, who ruled the Mauryan Empire between 273 and 232 BCE. In his rock edicts and pillar inscriptions, Ashoka referred to himself as 'Devanampiyatissa' (Beloved-of-the-Gods) Sidhartha Anuyaka (Sidharth, son of Anuruddha) or just Sidhartha.
